A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CondAmbigQA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison. Revised experimental settings limit direct comparison of performance values, but do not prevent comparison of the reported content.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, controlled condition-guidance comparisons, scaling analyses, and scored case studies in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, condition-guidance and closed-book experiments, ALCE-ASQA evaluation, and human validation of G-Eval in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix D changes the inference instruction from identifying up to three conditions to up to five, extending the permitted condition enumeration. The underlying retrieval, condition identification, conditional answering, and citation procedure remains intact; expanded annotation explanations do not establish a new annotation algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds a reported no-retrieval scenario and evaluation on 948 questions from the parent ALCE-ASQA benchmark using its DPR passages without ground-truth condition annotations (Sections 5.6 and 5.8). Coverage remains ambiguous factual QA. Expanding CondAmbigQA from 200 to 2,000 instances is principally a sample-size change.

E2.justification: DeepSeek-R1 (7B) joins the evaluated model set. The three-way condition-guidance comparison also expands from five local models in v1 Figure 5 to include GPT-4o and GLM4-plus in v2 Figure 4. Those two API models already appeared in v1's scaling analysis.

E3.justification: The benchmark expands from 200 to 2,000 instances. Citation Score changes its denominator from ground-truth citations to generated citations, and v2 adds signed Count Difference and a count-penalized Combined Score. Appendix D raises condition and baseline citation limits from three to five. New closed-book, external-dataset, and human-evaluation experiments introduce additional protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds a closed-book ablation (Table 3), condition–answer correlation analysis (Figure 5), and comparison of G-Eval with human judgments (Appendix E). Appendix F replaces v1's Ranch-centered case analysis and other examples with detailed city-comparison and color-TV cases, including analysis of DeepSeek's reasoning and failures. Scaling analysis is retained and revised.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained mean and standard-deviation reporting, v2 introduces statistical checks of annotation agreement, evaluator reliability, and the condition–answer relationship. These include Cohen's kappa approximately 0.72 and Pearson/Spearman correlations with p-values, including the 20-example human study in Appendix E. Neither version provides repeated-run or seed counts.

E6.justification: Main numerical results and rankings are extensively replaced: Gemma2's Answer Score is 0.306 in v1 Table 2 and 0.203 in v2 Table 2; DeepSeek-R1 has v2's highest local Answer Score at 0.293. V2 also reports ALCE-ASQA scores of 0.374 without conditions and 0.471 with conditions. Changed sample sizes, prompts, and scoring preclude interpreting cross-version differences as same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: The citation formula changes from intersection divided by reference-citation count (v1 Equation 4) to intersection divided by predicted-citation count (v2 Equation 1), changing recall to precision despite v2's 'recall-focused' description. V1's absolute answer-count-error definition is replaced by raw-count and signed-difference definitions; raw counts were already plotted in v1. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution of explicit conditions and human–LLM annotation remains. V2 increases the claimed benchmark size to 2,000 and revises abstract improvements from 20% plus 5% to 11.75% plus 7.15%. V1's broad claim that ambiguity resolution follows scaling laws becomes a narrower introductory claim about larger proprietary models outperforming smaller models.

C2.justification: V1 interprets citation generation as benefiting little from scaling and suggests diminishing returns; v2 emphasizes GPT-4o's citation advantage and interprets answer-count differences as precision-versus-coverage strategies. It also discusses why DeepSeek reasoning fails to close the capability gap. Expanded limitations address resource constraints, passage-reference dependence, subjective queries, deployment latency, and unhandled conflicting or adversarial evidence.

D1.justification: V2 adds annotator-team composition, annotation cost and time, licensing information, and access information for CondAmbigQA-2K. Conversely, it omits v1's top-20 retrieval specification, BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 embedding identifier, WhereIsAI corpus identifier, and named GPT4-mini evaluator. These materially change reproducibility documentation without establishing that the omitted underlying components were changed.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused, adding Chain-of-Draft, PSPO, adaptive QA, conflicting-context QA, retrieval credibility, and evaluator-instruction adherence. V1's explicit Grice/Levinson pragmatics grounding and extensive multi-agent discussion are removed. The central positioning against AmbigQA, ASQA, and APA remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten and condensed. Results are reorganized into separate condition, answer, citation, scaling, and additional-experiment subsections. Limitations become a standalone section, case-study discussion is reworked into Appendix F, and Appendix A's illustrative example is replaced. These exceed simple additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, substantially redesigns and consolidates performance plots, and expands Table 2 with API/local groupings, averages, combined scores, and count differences. It adds the correlation scatterplot and ablation, human-validation, and case-study tables. Retained appendix prompts are reformatted into numbered tables, and the annotation workflow graphic is revised.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens evaluation and adds a useful first human check of G-Eval, addressing limitations of v1's evidence. However, it removes retrieval and evaluator specifications and leaves Combined Score weights and penalties unspecified. Table 3 describes condition-based results as retrieval-free while repeating Figure 4's RAG answer scores without explanation; it also reports +161% for Mistral's 0.17-to-0.29 change, approximately 71%. These unresolved reliability and reproducibility problems prevent a confident judgment that the added evidence produces a net quality improvement.
